newsitem.title: MEXICO: Ten consortia vying for Mexico Toluca natgas site.
newsitem.headline: Ten consortia vying for Mexico Toluca natgas site.

text.p: Ten consortia have filed to bid for natural gas distribution rights in the Mexican industrial centre Toluca, the president of the Energy Regulatory Commission (CRE) said on Tuesday.
Bids for the coveted site were due on Monday, but CRE president Hector Olea said not all of the consortia that had applied to bid would decide to turn them in.
The 30-year concession will be awarded by July 9, the CRE has said. Toluca is 66 miles west of Mexico City, and accounts for two percent of national gross domestic product.

Toluca is considered the most attractive of the regions offered so far for natural gas distribution. Also being eyed are concessions for supplying the fuel in Mexico City and Monterrey, scheduled for later in the year.
Olea also said the CRE would announce the winning bidder for the Hermosillo natural gas region before the end of the month, ahead of the scheduled May 7.
The commission was reviewing bids from KN Energy Inc and from Argentina's private Compania General de Combustibles, he said.
Mexico is in the process of auctioning off rights to distribute natural gas as part of an effort to boost infrastructure and use of the fuel.
All natural gas in Mexico is supplied by state oil and gas monopoly Petroleos Mexicanos (Pemex).
